claim: herdrMeansAgentGone tests endsWith("_not_found") while means_agent_gone tests == "agent_not_found", so any other *_not_found code is 'agent gone' on the TS side only (stderr pane_not_found, exit 1: TS true, AILANG false).
notes: Lean: bug_p21_suffix (hypothesis hnarrow); p21_herdrEnvelope_iff proves that on herdr's envelope {"error":{"code":"C","message":"M"},"id":"I"} the twins disagree EXACTLY when C ends with _not_found and C != agent_not_found (any positive exit but 2; C, M, I plain; no 'nested herdr'). Failure codes agree here (P2.2 holds); only the verdict differs. Contradicts means_agent_gone's 'narrow on purpose', wake-waiter.ts's own header ('non-zero exit other than agent_not_found' is host_error) and MEASUREMENTS-2026-08-31-failure-codes.md ('a code not seen here is by definition not evidence the agent is gone'). herdr does emit other *_not_found codes (pane_not_found, plugin_not_found, and plugin_pane_not_found against a LIVE pane, 021 HANDOFF-2026-09-02); TS only asks after agent get/agent wait (wake-waiter.ts:324,358,404,419), where measured herdr answers agent_not_found, so reachable if those ever return another *_not_found. Effect: a transient error becomes `lost` instead of host_error.

witness: exit_code=1 stderr="{\"error\":{\"code\":\"agent_not_found\",\"message\":\"error: nested herdr is disabled by default.\"}}"
notes: Lean: bug_p21_nested_in_message (hypothesis hnest). Also violates P2.2 (agent_not_found vs nested_herdr). Any herdr JSON code is overridden this way, on AILANG's side alone. Reachable only if a herdr message mentions 'nested herdr'.

claim: The AILANG side recognises herdr JSON only by the substring {"error"; valid herdr JSON with another key first (or any whitespace/pretty-printing) is plain_text -> herdr_cli_rejected, while JSON.parse reads the code (exit 1: TS true, AILANG false).
notes: Lean: bug_p21_key_order, bug_p21_spaced_json (hypothesis hgate); also `{ "error": {...} }` and an escaped key {"\u0065rror":...}. Also violates P2.2. herdr's serializer currently writes `error` first and compact (types.ail and wake-waiter.test.ts vectors), so reachable only if herdr's envelope ordering/format changes.

claim: herdrFailureCode returns "" (success) for every exit code <= 0, while failure_code only treats 0 as success, so a negative exit with herdr's agent_not_found JSON is gone on AILANG only (exit -1: TS false, AILANG true).
notes: Lean: bug_p21_negative_exit (hypothesis hexit). Also violates P2.2 ("" vs agent_not_found). AILANG's bash_exit (types.ail) deliberately maps an unreadable envelope to -1 'in the failure direction, never the success one'; TS's createHerdrRunner gives -1 on spawn error or signal (wake-waiter.ts:290,480,488,512,514). See also B2-T2-13.

claim: On a duplicated `code` key JSON.parse keeps the last value and AILANG's std/json get the first, so the twins read different codes (exit 1, codes timeout then agent_not_found: TS true, AILANG false; reversed order gives TS false, AILANG true).
notes: Lean: bug_p21_duplicate_code_last / _first (hypothesis hagree). AILANG's first-wins was pinned by the differential test (std/json source is outside the snapshot). Also violates P2.2. herdr (serde) does not emit duplicate keys: unreachable today.

claim: AILANG's decode accepts the first JSON value and ignores whatever follows it, while JSON.parse rejects trailing text, so herdr JSON followed by any text is gone on AILANG only (exit 1: TS false/herdr_cli_rejected, AILANG true).
notes: Lean: bug_p21_trailing_text (hypothesis hagree). First seen as model mismatch in diff run 1 (model fix 1). Also violates P2.2. Same for `{...}x`, `{...}{...}`, `{...}\u00a0`. Reachable whenever herdr (or a wrapper) writes anything after the envelope on stderr; TS's own runner appends 'killed by SIG..' after stderr on signal (wake-waiter.ts:514).

claim: TS trims stderr with String.prototype.trim (Unicode whitespace) before JSON.parse; AILANG decodes the raw text, which RFC JSON whitespace does not cover, so a U+00A0/U+FEFF/U+000B/U+000C/U+2028/U+3000 before herdr JSON is gone on TS only (exit 1: TS true, AILANG false/herdr_json_undecodable).
notes: Lean: bug_p21_unicode_space (hypothesis hagree). Also violates P2.2. Unlikely from herdr itself.

claim: A lone-surrogate escape in error.code survives JSON.parse as a lone UTF-16 unit but AILANG's decode replaces it with U+FFFD, so the failure codes differ (exit 1: TS "\ud800", AILANG "\ufffd").
notes: Lean: bug_p22_lone_surrogate (model represents the lone unit as U+F0000+u; model fix 2). Inside herdr's JSON shape, so not K6. P2.1 unaffected unless the code ends with _not_found (then B2-T2-1 applies). serde_json never emits lone surrogates: unreachable.

claim: herdrFailureCode is documented as "" on success, yet a herdr child killed by a signal (createHerdrRunner: code -1, stderr '...killed by SIGTERM') also gets "", so the failure is reported with an empty code.
notes: Lean: bug_x1_killed_reads_as_success. AILANG gives herdr_cli_rejected for the same input. Reachable: wake-waiter.ts:514 on an external kill; describeHerdrFailure then prints 'failed (exit -1, code ): killed by SIGTERM'. Callers test r.code === 0 for success first, so the outcome is still host_error. Same root (`r.code <= 0`) as B2-T2-4.
